label: Integrating Factor Method
subgoals: Write the equation as y' + P(x) y = Q(x)
Multiply through so the left side is (mu y)'

slice.rule: Put the equation in the form $y' + P(x)\,y = Q(x)$. The integrating factor $\mu(x) = e^{\int P(x)\,dx}$ makes the left side an exact derivative: $(\mu y)' = \mu Q$. Then $y = \dfrac{1}{\mu}\left(\int \mu Q\,dx + C\right)$.
slice.note: Divide by the coefficient of $y'$ first; $P$ is read off only from the standard form.

label: Worked linear solve
subgoals: Divide back by mu and keep C

slice.rule: After multiplying by $\mu$, integrate both sides, then divide by $\mu$; the constant stays inside the bracket, so it gets divided by $\mu$ too.

examples.says: $e^{2x} y = \int e^{3x}\,dx = \tfrac13 e^{3x} + C$, so $y = \tfrac13 e^{x} + C e^{-2x}$

slice.rule: An initial condition $y(x_0) = y_0$ fixes $C$: substitute after finding the general solution.
